---
title: "Cognitive neuroscience"
description: "Mathematical modelling, fMRI and EEG to understand human decision making, and how decision processes differ in adults with ADHD"
aliases:
  - /project/cogneuro/
---

In this research line I used and sometimes still use mathematical modelling of cognitive processes, functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), and EEG to understand how humans make decisions, and how decision processes are different in adults with ADHD.

In one paper, colleagues and I used the drift diffusion model of decision making and fMRI to describe how [costs and benefits are represented in the brain](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21118983/) during decision making. In a related paper we looked for [representations of probabilistic evidence](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20439711/).

I've also done [some](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20510376/) [work](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19822738/) on reinfocement learning in general, and how it is influenced by social learning, leading to the proposal that [following reward can in itself be rewarding](https://journals.plos.org/plosbiology/article?id=10.1371/journal.pbio.1001089). Some og this work has clear markers of a past time, like the [small-sample target-gene study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19822738/). While this was exciting work at the time, I would approach this research differently today.

More recently I have used quantitative models of decision making to understand decision making in ADHD. [This](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25477020/) and [this](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27608958/) review describe the general idea. And here we use the [drift diffusion model of decision making as a choice model for reinforcement learning](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27966103/) in an attempt to described the effect of ADHD medication on decision making and learning.
